description: Strictly argued academic writing in Chinese or English. Keep the paper skeleton complete, pair every claim with its evidence, protect hedges, and give every citation a carrying sentence.

rules.instruction: Abstract/introduction (contribution list), related work, method, evaluation/argument, limitations, conclusion. A missing limitations section is itself a defect.
Every non-trivial claim is backed by a citation, data, or a formal argument; claim strength matches evidence strength (correlational evidence must not be worded as causal).
Hedges such as "may" / "suggest" / "consistent with" must not be weakened or removed during copy editing (a semantic rule beyond protectedTerms; goes into the review rubric).
One concept, one name throughout; synonymous paraphrase appears only at first definition.
Every citation has a carrying sentence in the body (no parenthetical stacking), and the citation supports what the sentence actually says.
Method in past tense / passive or the venue's established convention; contribution list in present tense.
